law_name: Act revoking Hungary's withdrawal from the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
description: Government bill tabled on 25 May 2026 and adopted on 27 May under a fast-track procedure (133 votes in favour), repealing the Orbán government's 2025 decision to leave the ICC days before the withdrawal was due to take effect on 2 June 2026. On 29 May 2026 the government notified the UN Secretary-General that it was withdrawing its notice of withdrawal.
significance: One of the new government's first legislative acts; it kept Hungary a State Party to the ICC and reversed a high-profile Orbán-era foreign-policy decision.

law_name: 16th amendment to the Fundamental Law of Hungary (Alaptörvény tizenhatodik módosítása)
description: Adopted on 15 June 2026 (135 votes to 50, 6 abstentions, according to most reports). It bars anyone from serving more than eight years as prime minister, consecutively or not, counting terms since 1990, which rules out a return by Viktor Orbán and also binds Magyar. It also addressed the public-interest asset-management foundations created under Orbán and prepared the abolition of the Sovereignty Protection Office.
significance: Delivered the Tisza pledge of a two-term limit for prime ministers and began dismantling Orbán-era institutions.

law_name: Public-media reform act (replacement of MTVA and Duna Média)
description: Tisza bill adopted in late June 2026 by 145 votes to 39 (Fidesz–KDNP against, Mi Hazánk in favour). It replaces MTVA and the Duna Média Service with Magyar Rádió és Televízió and an independent national news agency (MTI), requires the incumbent leadership to step down, provides for executives to be chosen by open competition and for an Independent Public Media Council, and creates a press fund for independent journalism.
significance: Basis for the suspension of public-media news on 7 July 2026 and the restructuring of the broadcaster used by Fidesz governments since 2010.

law_name: 17th amendment to the Fundamental Law of Hungary (Alaptörvény tizenhetedik módosítása)
description: Adopted in July 2026 by 139 votes to 6. It ended the mandate of President Tamás Sulyok, who signed it on 18 July 2026 and left office on 20 July; Speaker Ágnes Forsthoffer then exercised the president's powers until parliament elected András Baka on 11 August 2026.
significance: The most contested of the government's constitutional changes: Fidesz called it illegitimate, while Magyar presented it as part of the 'system change' endorsed by voters.

law_name: Act XXXIV of 2026 on the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (2026. évi XXXIV. törvény a Nemzeti Vagyonvisszaszerzési és Vagyonvédelmi Hivatalról)
description: Adopted on 28 July 2026 (143 votes to 47 on the qualified-majority provisions) and in force from 29 July 2026, with most criminal-procedure powers applying from 27 September 2026. It creates an office empowered to investigate abuses of public property and help recover unlawfully acquired assets. Its first head, Anna Unger, was elected on 28 August 2026.
significance: Delivers a central anti-corruption pledge of the Tisza programme; the Hungarian Helsinki Committee criticised the draft's limited judicial review and Fidesz announced a Constitutional Court challenge.

law_name: Accession to the European Public Prosecutor's Office (confirmed by Commission Decision (EU) 2026/1701)
description: The government requested to join the enhanced cooperation on the EPPO at the end of May 2026; the European Commission confirmed Hungary's participation on 10 July 2026 and Hungary became a participating Member State in early August 2026. The EPPO can consider offences committed after 1 June 2021 and becomes operational in Hungary once a European Prosecutor for Hungary is appointed.
significance: Reversed the Orbán governments' refusal to join the EPPO and supported the release of frozen EU funds.

law_name: Government Decree 92/2026 (VI. 5.) amending Government Decree 450/2024 on guest workers
description: In force from 6 June 2026, the decree left no third country whose citizens may obtain a guest-worker residence permit, ending new applications under that scheme, while leaving the separate residence permit for employment purposes and the extension of existing permits in place. Government Decision 1153/2026 (V. 18.) ordered a wider review of the rules on third-country workers.
significance: Partial implementation of the campaign pledge to halt the import of non-European guest workers from 1 June 2026.

description: Adopted on 13 October 2026 by 139 votes to 51 (Fidesz against) after the Court of Justice of the EU found the 2021 law incompatible with EU law. It removes the ban on the 'portrayal' or 'promotion' of sexual and gender diversity to minors and replaces it with a general rule protecting under-18s from material that can seriously impair their development. Other provisions, including the ban on adoption by same-sex couples, the constitutional language and the assembly-law restrictions used against Pride events, were not changed by this vote.
significance: First rollback of Orbán-era anti-LGBTQ legislation; Magyar framed it as bringing Hungary in line with EU law.
